_readme: THE OUTLET'S CONTENT, AS DATA. `seed/outlet.mjs` reads this file and drives the port; no rule about a
product, a price or a placement lives in that script. Same division as `catalog.json` beside it.
WHAT THIS SLICE (D2) HAD TO DECIDE, BECAUSE THE TWO SOURCES DISAGREE:
· The ARTBOARD (`Home Outlet.dc.html`) names eight products and prices them — 'Tênis Velocity 9' at
R$ 279,90 was R$ 909,90, and so on down both shelves. Those names are the design's own fiction: no
catalogue in this house carries them, and the brief says not to invent product.
· The INSTANCE's catalogue (the reference dataset the storefront's own menu was curated against) carries
2 790 real products with real photographs, real size grids and real technical sheets.
So the PRODUCTS are real ones from that catalogue and the MERCHANDISING is the artboard's: its eight
de/por pairs, in its order, across its two shelves. Nothing is invented; the design decides what a
shopper sees and the catalogue decides what a shopper buys.
MONEY IS IN CENTS, always, never a float. `amount: 27990` is R$ 279,90. Every pair below is one of the
artboard's, and the discounts it drew are 60–69% — which is what makes the announcement bar's 'Até 70%
OFF' a fact about this catalogue rather than a sentence somebody typed.
`stock` IS THE SCARCITY, and it is why the `acabando` COLLECTION can be called what it is called. A number
sets every SKU of that product; a LIST sets them one by one, in the SKU order below — that is how a shoe
in `acabando` ends up with two units in 39, none in 41 and one in 43. The default warehouse's oversell
policy is `block`, so a zero really is a size a shopper cannot buy. (03/09, pk5: the collection is still
here and still reachable at `/collection/acabando`; what left is the SHELF that showed it on the home.)
★★ THE MENU IS THE ASSORTMENT'S CONTRACT (A40, decided by the Renan on 2026-09-02). The vanilla vitrine's
header menu is HAND-CURATED in the kit (`packages/storefront-kit/src/subtemplates/header/navTree.ts`), and
the Outlet wears it whole: 5 top categories, 28 leaves, 33 links. Any store served by the vanilla therefore
has to CARRY those categories or it ships links into the void — measured before this change: 8 products in 4
leaves, and 27 of the 33 links landing on an empty list. His ruling was to POPULATE, never to add a mechanism
to the shared storefront:
"Como é storefront provavelmente seria um fork ... Criar mais mecanismos para o storefront não é a
solução ... Nesse caso prefiro popular as mesmas categorias na demo, pois também fica mais bacana."
So `categories` below MIRRORS that curated tree, and every leaf of it carries at least one published product.
⚠️ THE MIRROR IS THE FRAGILE PART: nothing in this repository compiles against `navTree.ts`. A leaf added
there and not here is a dead link again, and only a human notices. `seed/outlet.test.mjs` guards the half
that IS checkable — that every leaf DECLARED here has a product, and that every product names a declared
leaf.
THE CATEGORIES ARE THE DATASET'S, PATH FOR PATH, NAME FOR NAME, HANDLE FOR HANDLE — and that is not a
courtesy, it is what keeps two seeds from fighting. `seed/forge.mjs` creates the very same 33 from the
mounted dataset, looking each one up BY PATH first; and `catalog.product.categorize` refuses a SECOND primary
category on a product. Whichever of the two seeds runs first wins the create and the other reuses it, and the
primary they both write is the same row. Diverge on a path here and that becomes a `validation_failed` in
whichever runs second.
THE PRODUCTS ARE THE DATASET'S TOO — real catalogue, real photograph, real size grid — re-priced for a
clearance store. The `de` is the dataset's own figure, so it is plausible for the shoe; the `por` is this
file's. That is also why the handles must never be invented: `seed/forge.mjs` publishes all 2790 into the
`forge` store and finds these already there, by handle, and leaves them alone.
★ THE DISCOUNT IS A RULE, NOT A TASTE (A40). The announcement band promises "Até 70% OFF" and the catalogue
has to honour it: EVERY product carries `compare_at_amount`, the floor is 30%, the ceiling is the band's own
70%, the bulk sits between 40 and 60, and a few sit near the ceiling as the bait. `seed/outlet.test.mjs`
fails on a product that has no `de`, or whose pair falls outside 30–70 — the guard reads the RESULT (the two
figures) and not a table of intentions.
⛔⛔ AND THE `de` IS NOT WRITTEN WHEN THE PRODUCT IS CREATED — IT CANNOT BE. The birth runs 8 · the curated
seed → 9 · the massive one-shot → 10 · the past → 11 · the window. Step 9 (`apps/api/src/seed-media.ts`)
converges every SKU it matches BY CODE to the DATASET's `compare_at_amount ?? null`, and leaves `amount`
alone — and every product below is a dataset product with the dataset's own SKU codes, which is exactly what
makes it realistic. So a discount written in phase 8 is nulled in phase 9, in silence, leaving low prices and
no visible discount: the "2 of the 8" the Renan reported. The figures below are therefore applied by
`priceOutlet()` in the WINDOW phase, after that step has spoken. `seed/outlet.test.mjs` guards the ORDER as
well as the data — a data guard alone stays green while the shop shows nothing.
★★ 03/09 — THE SHOP NOW CARRIES CHILDREN'S SHOES, AND EVERY LABEL ITS HOME PROMOTES (s2-2, s2-4). Two
findings of the same shape as A40's: a page promising something the assortment did not have.
· The «OUTLET KIDS · R$ 149,90» piece linked to a collection of 22 ADULT products, and the whole
catalogue held no `genero: Infantil` at all — so the header's «Infantil» link and the banner both led
nowhere. 16 children's products now sit in a THIRD collection, `outlet-kids`, one per menu leaf that
can hold one; the banner and a new shelf both point at it. The art's own number is a real product:
the pink adidas VL Court in the piece is priced at its de R$ 299,90 / por R$ 149,90.
· 4 of the 8 «Marcas que amamos» tiles landed on an empty list, because that list is a literal in the
VITRINE and resolves against the TENANT's brands. `featured_brands` below mirrors it and the shop now
stocks all eight. See `_featured_brands_why`.
EVERY PRODUCT DECLARES ITS `brand`, AND THIS SEED STILL WRITES NONE — the field is the dataset's answer,
copied here so a guard can ask «does the shop carry the label its home is promoting?» without a hand-
written list of the ones somebody once fixed. Same standing as `category`: a mirror of the dataset that
the tests read and the port never receives. (`categorize` fails loudly when `category` drifts, because the
kernel refuses a second primary; NOTHING fails when `brand` drifts — that one is on the reader.)
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, AND IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT:
· NO BRANDS WRITTEN. `catalog.brand.create` is the dataset seed's, and it runs after this one; a `brand_id`
here would be a second author for 351 rows this file does not own.
⚠️ AND THE OLD COST WRITTEN HERE — «a PDP with no brand line on these products» — IS FALSE, measured
twice. The demo-data install re-asserts `brand_id` on a product it finds ALREADY THERE, by handle
(`extensions/demo-data/populate.ts`, the `catalog.product.update` after the reuse branch), and every
product below is one of its own. The QA saw the consequence from the other side: `/b/nike` inside the
outlet lists product. So these products DO wear their label — this file simply is not the author.
That is exactly why `brand` can be declared here as data and never sent to the port.
· NO PROMOTION ROWS. The de/por a shopper sees is `compare_at_amount`, which is the operator's own
figure on the SKU — not a promotion engine rule. The artboard shows struck-through prices and a
discount tag, and that is exactly what this produces.
· NO CATEGORY BANNER ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE, and "take the category banners off the Outlet" is NOT done
here — see the note at the end.
THE PHOTOS in `outlet-media/` come from that same reference dataset (the artboard's own product shots
are `fotos teste/*.webp` inside the design project, and its five mosaic tiles are empty placeholders —
there is no banner artwork in the design to extract). Cover plus three gallery frames per product; the
six banners are the dataset's curated campaign art.

⚠️ ONE TILE IS CROPPED, AND IT IS THE LIBRARY THAT IS SHORT, NOT THE GRID. The artboard's mosaic is two proportions — two near-square cells (296x300) and three wide ones — and this instance's banner art holds four campaigns, of which exactly ONE is square (`banner-bota`), plus two shelf-shaped pieces and one that carries LOREM IPSUM in the artwork itself (`banner-sportswear`, unusable in front of anybody). So the second square cell takes the adventure piece (462x373) and loses about 10% off each side of its headline. The alternative was the same campaign twice in one mosaic in its two official crops, which reads as a bug in the data rather than as merchandising — and cropping to fill is what the block's own manifest says a tile does with art of another proportion. The fix is one square campaign in the library, not a change here.
⚠️ THE ONE THING A40 ASKED FOR THAT THIS FILE CANNOT DO: "banners de categorias pode tirar do outlet".
Measured on the bench: the Outlet's composition holds NO category banner — every banner tile it places links
to a `/collection/*`, and there is not one `list.*` placement in the store. The banner a shopper actually
meets is the CATEGORY'S OWN rich art (`category.banner`, drawn by the list template as `template_banner`),
and the `category` row is TENANT-scoped: 3 of the 33 carry one (`tenis`, `sandalias`, `acessorios`), all
written by `seed/forge.mjs` from the dataset, and all shared with the `forge` store where they are wanted.
Stripping them would strip them from both shops. So it is reported, not guessed at.
⚠️ AND ONE PIECE OF PROSE IN `outlet.mjs` IS FALSE AND IS LEFT FOR ITS OWNER TO FIX: `compose()` says the
two fixed sections "render nothing here because this store has neither". Measured on the bench BEFORE this
change — the Outlet's home already served `data-testid="home-categories"` (five tiles) and
`data-testid="home-brands"`, because both reads are over TENANT rows: the 33 categories and the 351 brands
`seed/forge.mjs` writes reach every store of the tenant whatever its assortment. A40 keeps «Compre por
categoria» on this page deliberately; what changes here is that its five tiles now lead somewhere.

_why: ★ HALF OF THIS SENTENCE WAS A LIE, MEASURED 02/09, AND IT WAS THE HALF WITH A NUMBER IN IT.
It used to read «Outlet oficial · Até 70% OFF · Frete grátis acima de R$ 600», and the two halves were
not equally true:
· «Até 70% OFF» ✅ — the catalogue's real discount range is 33–70%, ceiling exactly 70. The test below
reads that ceiling OFF THIS SENTENCE and holds every price under it.
· «Frete grátis acima de R$ 600» ⛔ — the outlet has ONE active promotion (10% on the first purchase)
and NONE of freight. There is no R$ 600 and there never was; the shop was advertising something the
kernel could not do, on the first line of every page.
⇒ The freight promise is GONE rather than backed by a new promotion: he asked for «uma de desconto» in
this shop, not for a second freight rule. The words are his: «Aproveita: até 70% OFF».
★ AND THE COUPLING IS DELIBERATE — DO NOT BREAK IT. `seed/outlet.test.mjs` derives the discount ceiling
from the `%` in this very sentence, so LOWERING the promise tightens the guard by itself and no price
can drift above what the page claims. It is the opposite of a hand-written list: the sentence and the
catalogue cannot disagree without somebody going red.

_pages_why: ★★ THE SEVEN INSTITUTIONAL PAGES OF THE OUTLET — AND THE HALF OF THEM THIS FILE CANNOT WRITE.
MEASURED 05/09 ON THE BENCH, seven requests each: the `forge` store answers 200 at /contato, /entrega,
/faq, /privacidade, /sobre, /termos and /trocas-e-devolucoes; the OUTLET answered 404 at all seven, in
the same tenant. The institutional sidebar the storefront draws on those pages is HARDCODED with the
same seven links (`storefront-coffee/src/templates/cms/PageView.tsx:13-21`, a byte-identical copy of the
reference storefront's), so a shopper who reached one of them from the Outlet was handed seven dead
links. That is what this block ends.
⛔⛔ AND THE TEXT ON THOSE PAGES IS NOT DATA — NOT HERE, AND NOT ANYWHERE. `content.page.create` writes
the page CARD only: slug, title, template_key, meta_title, meta_description, published. There is no body
column and it is a product decision, written at `packages/core/src/commands/page.ts:1-3` («the CONTENT is
the theme template's code (yellow zone), never stored here»). The prose comes from ONE component per
`template_key`, in the storefront image, resolved by a registry with NO STORE AXIS
(`apps/storefront/src/templates/cms/registry.ts:22-32`), and the Outlet is served by the vanilla image
(`caddy/Caddyfile.local:150-151`). So the Outlet's /trocas-e-devolucoes renders, word for word, the same
paragraphs as the Forge store's — verified live on the bench, «7 dias corridos» and all.
⇒ THE OWNER ASKED FOR TEXT OF ITS OWN («faz sentido ser diferente para outlet») AND THIS SLICE COULD
ONLY DELIVER PART OF IT. What is genuinely the Outlet's here is the `title` — which the template prints
as the page's <h1> — and the two meta fields. The BODY needs one of two things this repository may not
do: a store axis on the CMS template registry, or a body on the page card. Both are the product's, both
are in the other repo, and the slice report names them.
★ SO EVERY `meta_description` BELOW IS TRUE OF THE PAGE THAT WILL ACTUALLY RENDER. It was written
against the vanilla templates as they stand, clause by clause: nothing here promises a paragraph the
shared body does not carry. A description that advertised outlet-specific answers over the reference
FAQ would be exactly the species of prose this repository keeps paying for.
⚠️ AND THE OUTLET IS NOT A SECONDS SHOP. The brief supposed «peça de ponta de estoque / segunda linha»;
the dataset says otherwise and the dataset wins. The products here ARE the Forge store's products, the
dataset's real catalogue with real photographs and real size grids, re-priced for a clearance store (the
`_readme` above says so, and `seed/forge.mjs` publishes the very same handles into `forge`). What is
scarce is the SIZE GRID — that is what the `acabando` collection is named for. No copy below claims a
defect, an avaria or a second line, because the catalogue has none.
★ `privacidade` AND `termos` KEEP THE LOJA-MÃE'S TITLE ON PURPOSE. A privacy policy or a terms page that
reads differently per storefront is a LEGAL claim nobody in this house made, and inventing a variation
to look less duplicated would be decoration with a liability attached. The two shops share the tenant,
the customer records and the carriers; those two pages say the same thing because they are the same
thing.
★ THE CARRIERS CLAIM IN `entrega` IS MEASURED, not flattery: `read.shipping_methods_admin` has no store
parameter and `seed/box.json` declares delivery PER TENANT, so the Outlet ships on the same methods the
Forge store does. `bin/verify-seed.mjs` reads that same list without a store filter.

_home_why: ★★ 02/09 — THE BLOCKS OF THE HOME ALL LIVE IN ONE SLOT, AND THAT IS THE TEMPLATE'S DOING.
(03/09, pk5: they are THREE — the mosaic, «Quase de graça» and «Outlet Kids». «Acabando!» left the home
and the kids ART became that shelf's own promo picture; see the shelf's `_why` for his words.)
He asked for this order: «Compre por categoria» → the banner mosaic → «Quase de graça» → «Acabando»
(with its banner) → «Marcas que amamos». (03/09, pk5: «Acabando» left the home — see the «Outlet Kids»
shelf's `_why`.) The reference home draws its sections in a FIXED order
(apps/storefront/src/templates/home/template.tsx:40-46) and only two of them are ours to move:
1 home.hero · 2 home.banner_strip · 3 home.below_shelf · 4 «Compre por categoria» (FIXED SECTION,
not a slot) · 5 home.below_categories · 6 «Marcas que amamos» (FIXED SECTION) · 7 home.below_brands
There is exactly ONE slot between the two fixed sections he named, so all of them go into it and the
ORDER IS `position`, not the slot name. A slot takes N blocks — the `forge` store already stacks two
shelves that way.
SO FOUR SLOTS ARE EMPTY ON PURPOSE — `home.hero`, `home.banner_strip`, `home.below_shelf` and
`home.below_brands` — and so is the whole PLP (`list.*`). They are not 'not done yet': putting the mosaic
back in `home.hero` would draw it ABOVE «Compre por categoria», which is the one thing he asked to change.
⚠️ A BANNER IS EITHER A BLOCK OF ITS OWN OR THE SHELF'S FIRST GRID CELL, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME THING.
A `banners/banner` block owns a LINE: it flows its tiles by their `width` percentage and whatever is left
of the 100% is white. A shelf's `banner_asset` is a CELL of the shelf's own five-column grid, spanning two
of the five beside three product cards. The 02/09 page moved the «Acabando» art out of its shelf into a
block, because what he asked for then was a banner AFTER the shelf; pk5 put the kids art back INSIDE the
shelf, because a picture that owns a line it cannot fill is the one that falls.
⚠️ AND `compose()` NOW GOVERNS THESE SLOTS RATHER THAN APPENDING TO THEM. With two `banners/banner` blocks
in ONE slot, 'is there a placement of this app+component in this slot?' stops identifying anything — and a
seed that only appends would leave the OLD home (hero + banner_strip + below_shelf) drawn above the new one
on every box that ran the previous version. See the header of that function.
_brand_why: THE STORE'S OWN MARK, and it is DATA rather than a token — which is the whole reason it is a block and
not a line in themes/outlet/tokens.css. A theme is colour, radius and typeface; a wordmark is content,
and the artboard's header says `forge` in white with `.outlet` painted in the accent. Without this
placement the shared kit prints its own literal `forge.` at the top of every page of a store that is
not Forge — measured on the bench of 2026-09-03, in light ink on the new dark band.
`text` + `tail` rather than `logo`: the app takes either, and this store has no logo FILE. The tail is
painted with the accent by the block's own stylesheet, so the two halves of the artboard's mark come
from one placement and no image at all.

_why: The five campaign pieces, in two rows: 50 + 25 + 25 fills the first line, 50 + 50 wraps to the second.
`width` is a PERCENTAGE of the row and `height` is PIXELS — the block's own vocabulary, not CSS.
THE HEIGHTS ARE DERIVED FROM THE ART, not chosen: at the storefront's ~1504px content column a 50% cell
is ~736px and a 25% cell ~352px. 1232x608 at 736 wide is 363 tall and a 600x600 at 352 wide is 352 —
so 360 is the row height that crops both by ~2%. The second row is 1228x440 at 736 wide = 264.
The frame is `overflow:hidden` + `object-fit:cover`, so a wrong height CROPS and never distorts.
⚠️ A FILE NAME LIED AND THE NAMES IN THIS REPO ARE THE MEASURED ONES. 'Banner Outlet 1 - Bota
Adventure 1228x600.png' is really 1232x608. It does not break anything — the block crops — but a name
that describes a size the file does not have is what sends the next person looking for a bug in the
layout.
★ 04/09 (A6) — THE CHILDREN'S PIECE WAS RE-CUT AND ITS NAME MOVED WITH IT. It used to be the
462x373-named file that measured 912x752; the art delivered on 04/09 is 912x736 and the repo's copy is
`banner-outlet-kids-912x736.png`. It is not one of the five mosaic tiles — it is the «Outlet Kids»
shelf's own promo cell (see that shelf's `_why`), so no height here describes it.
⚠️ `alt` HERE IS DOCUMENTATION AND REACHES NO PAGE — measured. The `banner` block's item schema has no alt
field (extensions/banners/manifest.ts) and the render hard-codes `alt=""` with the reason 'decorative'
(render.tsx:209). These five tiles carry prices and product names, so 'decorative' is not true of them; the
sentences are kept because they say what each piece IS, and the day the app grows the field they are ready.

shelves.title: Outlet Kids
shelves.banner_alt: Outlet Kids: grandes marcas, preços pequenos — de R$ 299,90 por R$ 149,90
_why: s2-8 — THE COMPANY THE «OUTLET KIDS» BANNER WAS MISSING, and it is a shelf rather than more art
because the art does not exist: `/collection/outlet-kids` is where both the picture and this shelf's
«Ver todos →» lead, and it is the same list.
★★★ 03/09 (pk5) — THE PICTURE IS THIS SHELF'S FIRST GRID CELL NOW, NOT A BLOCK OF ITS OWN, AND THAT
IS THE WHOLE FIX. He looked at the row and corrected the earlier diagnosis himself:
«Olhei na loja e está caindo na verdade, será que está no lugar errado? É melhor cortar um pouco do
que cair. E esse tipo de shelf que tem banner na verdade é banner + 3 e tem 4 produtos de kids...
Mas estranho que essa shelf já existia na loja normal de sapatos. O tamanho era só seguir o mesmo
de lá. Inclusive o tamanho do arquivo do banner usei o mesmo. Aquele funcionava bem.»
AND HE IS RIGHT THAT IT ALREADY EXISTED — twice. «Botas que acabaram de chegar» in the `forge` store
is exactly this shape (the mounted dataset's `storefront.json`: `banner` + `banner_link` +
`item_count: 3`), and THIS FILE ITSELF shipped it on 02/09, on the «Acabando!» shelf, with the same
three key names. The 02/09 rework moved the art OUT of the shelf into a `banners/banner` block because
what he asked for then was a picture AFTER the shelf. That is what started falling.
★ THE TWO VOCABULARIES ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, and this is the measurement (bench, 2026-09-03):
· AS A BANNER BLOCK the art owned a LINE and was flowed by a `width` PERCENTAGE. At `width: 33` a
lone tile filled 33% of its line and left 67% white — that is the «caindo».
· AS A SHELF BANNER it is a CELL of the shelf's own five-column grid, spanning two of the five
(`extensions/shelves/block.module.css`), with three product cards beside it: 2 + 3 = 5 of 5
columns, one row, nothing blank. Identical to the gabarito, measured the same way.
SO `width` AND `height` ARE GONE, AND THEIR OLD REASONS WITH THEM. A shelf banner declares neither:
the cell's width is two fifths of the row and its height is the PRODUCT CARDS' (`min-height: 100%`
over `object-fit: cover`). The art is therefore cropped to whatever the cards are tall — which is his
ruling, in his words: «é melhor cortar um pouco do que cair». The old `_why` argued the opposite (that
full width would decapitate the art, so the tile must stay at a third) and it is not kept as history:
a reason that has been overruled and is left lying next to the data is how the next person re-derives
the defect.
THE LINK GOES WHERE THE PROMISE IS. It used to point at `/collection/acabando` — 22 products, every
one of them adult (s2-2). It points at the children's assortment, the same list the «Ver todos →» of
this very shelf opens.
⚠️ `banner_alt` REACHES NO PAGE — measured, and it is kept for the same reason the mosaic's `alt` is:
the block hard-codes `alt=""` on the promo image (`extensions/shelves/block.tsx`), so this sentence
is documentation and the only machine-readable transcription of what the pixels promise. The de/por
guard below reads it.
★★ 03/09 (pk5) — «ACABANDO!» IS GONE FROM THE HOME AND THIS SHELF IS THE LAST BLOCK ON IT. His
words: «essa acabando pode tirar e deixar só a kids e a quase de graça que já está certo». The
COLLECTION stays — 26 products are still pinned to `acabando` and `/collection/acabando` is still a
list a shopper can reach; what was removed is the row on the home. It was a three-card shelf in a
five-column grid, i.e. two blank columns of its own (measured on the bench, 40% of its row).
★★ 04/09 (A6) — THE ART WAS RE-CUT TO THE CELL'S OWN PROPORTION. `Banner Outlet Infantil 912x736.png`
replaces the 912x752 piece and lands here as `banner-outlet-kids-912x736.png`. 912x736 is 1.239:1;
the cell it fills spans two of the five grid columns and is as tall as the product cards beside it, so
the closer the art's own ratio is to that box the less `object-fit: cover` has to throw away. Nothing
in this file states a size for it — the shelf banner declares neither `width` nor `height` (see above)
— so the ONLY thing the new file changes here is its name.
⛔ AND THE ROUNDED CORNER HE ASKED FOR IN THE SAME BREATH IS NOT DATA — MEASURED, 04/09. The frame is
the `shelves` app's `.banner` (`extensions/shelves/block.module.css:281`): `overflow: hidden` and NO
`border-radius`. Its neighbours on this very home ARE rounded, by the OTHER app — the `banners`
mosaic's `.frame` carries `border-radius: var(--radius-surface)`
(`extensions/banners/banners.module.css:69`). So the two pieces of art on one page disagree because
two apps disagree, and the repair is one declaration in the PRODUCT repository, not a byte here. A
theme cannot reach it either: `themes/outlet/tokens.css` carries `--r/-sm/-xs`, and a radius token no
rule reads paints nothing.

collections.name: Outlet Kids
_why: s2-2 — WHAT THE BANNER WAS PROMISING AND THE SHOP DID NOT HAVE. The «OUTLET KIDS · GRANDES MARCAS
PREÇO PEQUENO · R$ 149,90» piece linked to `/collection/acabando`: 22 products, every one of them
adult. This collection is the destination that makes the art true — it is where the banner and the
«Outlet Kids» shelf both point, and every product pinned to it carries `genero: Infantil`.
THE ART'S OWN NUMBER IS A PRODUCT, not a rounding. `adidas-kids-vl-court-3-0-shoes-little-kid-big-kid`
IS the pink suede shoe with the green stripes and the gum sole in the piece, and it is priced at the
figure the piece prints: de R$ 299,90, por R$ 149,90.

_featured_brands_why: ★★ 03/09 — s2-4: THE «Marcas que amamos» TILES ARE A HAND-CURATED LITERAL IN THE VITRINE, AND THIS IS ITS
MIRROR — exactly the arrangement `categories` above has with the header menu, for exactly the same reason.
The reference vitrine's home block picks eight brand slugs from a list written in its own source
`read.brands`, which answers for the TENANT. So a slug resolves — the tile renders, the wordmark shows —
whether or not THIS STORE carries a single product of it, and `/b/<slug>` under the outlet is then an
honest, empty list. Measured by the QA: 4 of the 8 (Johnston Murphy, Corral Boots, Columbia, Ugg) landed
on «0 produtos — Nada por aqui»; the other 4 had product because the outlet happened to carry it.
⛔ THE FIX IS NOT OURS TO MAKE IN THE VITRINE. `apps/storefront` is the forkable reference storefront and
the Renan has twice refused to grow a mechanism there to accommodate this shop — «prefiro popular as
mesmas categorias na demo». Deriving the eight from what the STORE stocks is a change to the product, and
it belongs upstream, on its own card. What is OURS is the assortment: this shop now carries at least one
product of every label its home promotes.
⚠️ THE MIRROR IS THE FRAGILE HALF, and nothing here compiles against it: this repository has no package
manager and no dependency on the storefront. A slug swapped over there and not here is an empty tile
again, and only a human notices — the same standing risk `categories` carries against `navTree.ts`.
